title: Invertible multiplication on a semiabelian group is finite etale surjective
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A semiabelian $k$-group algebraic space means a smooth separated finite-type commutative group object $G$ in algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] admitting an exact sequence $0\to T\to G\to A\to0$ of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site], where $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^t$ for some integer $t\geq0$ and $A/k$ is an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Here $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, group-object operations induce functorial group operations on $U$-points, and exactness means that $T$ is the kernel and sections of $A$ locally lift to $G$ for fppf coverings. Smoothness and finite type are tested on etale scheme charts, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $n\geq1$ be invertible in $k$, and let $[n]_G:G\to G$ denote the sum of $n$ copies of the identity under the group law. Then $[n]_G$ is representable, finite, etale and surjective. Explicitly, for every $k$-scheme $U$ and $y\in G(U)$ the sheaf fibre product $V=U\times_{y,G,[n]_G}G$ is represented by a scheme, and $V\to U$ is finite etale and surjective. Finite means affine with coordinate algebra a finite module, and etale is [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Section 8.21, printed p.152, and Theorem 12.9(b), printed pp.233–234; semiabelian extension consequence, to be proved by local trivialization of the torus torsor and descent. The split-torus map is given by the coordinate power maps.

proof.text: First record the coordinate calculation needed below. For any commutative $k$-algebra $B$ and units $u_1,\ldots,u_t\in B^\times$, form $C_0=B$ and $C_j=C_{j-1}[z_j]/(z_j^n-u_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], each $C_j$ is free over $C_{j-1}$ on $1,z_j,\ldots,z_j^{n-1}$. Moreover $z_j$ is a unit, with inverse $u_j^{-1}z_j^{n-1}$; consequently the derivative $nz_j^{n-1}$ is a unit. The derivative-localized algebra of [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] is therefore $C_j$ itself, and its spectrum is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}C_{j-1}$. Finite and etale composition give $\operatorname{Spec}C_t\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ finite etale. It is surjective: for each prime of $B$, in an algebraic closure of its residue field each polynomial $z_j^n-u_j$ has a nonzero root; choosing these roots gives a point of $\operatorname{Spec}C_t$ above that prime. Here existence of the algebraic closure and its roots is [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. This scheme represents the functor of $t$ units $z_j$ satisfying $z_j^n=u_j$, since $z_j$ is already invertible in $C_t$. For $t=0$ take $C_t=B$, so the map is the identity.

source.place: Tags 00UB (definition-standard-etale), 00UC (lemma-standard-etale); monic division; coordinate calculation for the split torus.

proof.text: Write $q:G\to A$ for the quotient in the given exact sequence. By [lem-sc-isogeny-facts], $[n]_A$ is finite flat surjective and an fppf covering. By [lem-sc-mult-n-etale-kernel], it is etale: invertibility of $n$ is precisely the required characteristic condition (in characteristic zero use $n>0$). These statements include the zero-dimensional abelian variety. Fix an arbitrary scheme $U/k$ and $y\in G(U)$. Define the scheme $W=U\times_{q(y),A,[n]_A}A$; it carries a section $a\in A(W)$ satisfying $[n]_Aa=q(y)|_W$. Finite and etale base-change permanence make $W\to U$ finite etale. Its surjectivity follows also because it is an fppf covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change].

The sheaf $V=U\times_{y,G,[n]_G}G$ is an fppf sheaf: its sections are pairs consisting of a map to $U$ and an $x$ with $[n]_Gx=y$, and matching such pairs glue uniquely in the two sheaves. There is a map $V\to W$ sending $x$ to $(u,q(x))$, since $q([n]_Gx)=[n]_Aq(x)$. Exactness in the hypothesis says that the section $a\in A(W)$ lifts to sections $g_i\in G(W_i)$ on an fppf covering of $W$. Refine by affine open covers and denote the resulting covering again by $\{W_i\to W\}$, with $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Composition and refinement of coverings are part of the site axioms. Put $d_i=y|_{W_i}-[n]_Gg_i$. Its image in $A(W_i)$ is zero, so the specified kernel identification gives a unique $d_i\in T(W_i)=(B_i^\times)^t$. This uses the hypothesis of exactness, not a claim that $q$ already has a scheme source.

source.place: Section 8.21, printed p.152, extension consequence: local lifting along the torus quotient; explicit fppf-sheaf argument.

proof.text: On every scheme over $W_i$, a section of $V\times_WW_i$ has $q(x)=a$, so $x-g_i$ lies in the kernel $T$ uniquely. Write $x=g_i+t$. The equation $[n]_Gx=y$ becomes $[n]_Tt=d_i$ because the group is commutative. Under $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^t$, this means $t_j^n=d_{ij}$ for all $j$. Thus $t\mapsto g_i+t$ is a natural isomorphism from the root functor constructed in step 1 (with $B=B_i$, $u_j=d_{ij}$) to $V\times_WW_i$; its inverse is $x\mapsto x-g_i$. The local source $P_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_{i,t}$ is consequently finite etale surjective over $W_i$. No restriction to field-valued points is made in these mutually inverse formulas.

source.place: Section 8.21, printed p.152, agent-written extension argument: translation identifies the lifted-quotient fibre with a split-torus power fibre.

proof.text: The local presentations of the fppf sheaf $V/W$ determine compatible scheme isomorphisms on $W_i\times_WW_j$, by [lem-trf-fppf-local-representations-fully-faithful]. Both maps identify the same section $x$ of $V$, so their composites on triple overlaps agree. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-fppf-descent] to these finite etale schemes $P_i/W_i$ and their overlap maps, obtaining a finite etale scheme $P\to W$ with $P\times_WW_i\simeq P_i$. The same full-faithfulness statement glues the local identifications to an isomorphism of fppf sheaves $h_P\simeq V$ over $W$. Surjectivity of $P\to W$ follows directly: a point of $W$ lifts to some $W_i$ because the covering is jointly surjective, and then to $P_i$ by step 1; its image in $P$ lies over the original point.

The composite $P\to W\to U$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and surjective by the two surjections. The isomorphism $h_P\simeq V$ preserves the maps to $W$, hence to $U$. Thus it represents exactly $U\times_{y,G,[n]_G}G$ with its projection to $U$. Since $U$ and $y$ were arbitrary, this proves scheme representability of $[n]_G$ and the asserted finite etale surjective property on every scheme test, which is the meaning of all four conclusions in the statement. This includes empty $U$.
